title: API 653 Training in Lake Charles: Tank Inspector Exam Prep
description: Self-paced API 653 exam prep for Lake Charles tank inspectors: Calcasieu River crude terminals, refinery and chemical tank farms, SPCC and breakout tanks.
h1: API 653 Training in Lake Charles: Aboveground Storage Tank Inspector Exam Prep for Calcasieu River Terminals, Refinery Tank Farms and Chemical Storage
html:
API 653 exam prep for tank inspectors in Lake Charles

Ships and barges bring crude up the Calcasieu River, refineries at Westlake and Lake Charles store it before and after processing, and the chemical plants keep caustic, intermediates and finished products in their own tank farms. Somebody has to inspect the floors, shells and roofs of all those tanks, decide whether a repair is needed and approve it, and in this part of Louisiana that person is usually expected to hold API 653. This page is for terminal and refinery inspectors, MFL floor-scanning and UT technicians, tank repair welders and supervisors, and engineers who look after tank farms.

There is no Atlantis classroom in Lake Charles. The API 653 course is self-paced and online, with an instructor answering questions as you work through API 653, API 650 and the recommended practices, so you can prepare around terminal operations and refinery turnarounds. The American Petroleum Institute sets the eligibility rules under Annex D of API 653, administers the examination at Prometric test centres and issues the certification. The course prepares you for that examination and is not a certification in itself; Atlantis is not an API-approved training provider.

Crude terminals on the Calcasieu River

The clearest public description of a local tank farm comes from Phillips 66 Partners' 2014 annual report. It described the Clifton Ridge terminal, on the Calcasieu River about ten miles from the Lake Charles refinery, as having 12 aboveground storage tanks with roughly 3.4 million barrels of total capacity and a single-berth ship dock whose average delivery was 512,000 barrels. The neighbouring Pecan Grove terminal had three tanks holding 142,000 barrels and a barge dock. A 2015 description of the system adds that Clifton Ridge receives crude by pipeline, barge, tanker and truck, and a 2020 profile of the refinery confirms that Phillips 66 owns the terminal.

Twelve tanks sharing 3.4 million barrels works out at more than 280,000 barrels each on average, so these are large-diameter crude tanks, the kind where floor condition, settlement and shell thickness in the bottom course drive the inspection plan. A terminal like this receives, stores and ships on a schedule set by cargoes rather than by the inspection calendar, which is why internal inspections are planned years ahead and why the inspector's interval calculation matters commercially as well as technically.

Refinery and chemical tank farms

  • Refineries. EIA's January 2026 survey lists the Phillips 66 refinery at Westlake and Calcasieu Refining in Lake Charles, and there is a large refinery in Sulphur as well. Each keeps crude, intermediate and product tankage. Louisiana's 2025 refinery report names Calcasieu Refining as an independent refiner, one that buys most of its crude on the open market rather than producing it.
  • Lube and specialty products. Excel Paralubes exchanges vacuum gas oil and distillate with the Phillips 66 refinery next door, and specialty products need their own tanks and segregation.
  • Chemical storage. GlobalData lists caustic soda, chlorine, ethylene dichloride and vinyl chloride among the products of Westlake's Lake Charles complex, and the olefins and polyethylene plants keep their own feeds and intermediates. Atmospheric tanks in this kind of service bring the chemistry into the inspection: caustic, acid and chlorinated products each change what an inspector looks for.
  • Closed units. In December 2025 Westlake announced the closure of its Lake Charles North vinyl chloride monomer plant, a diaphragm chlor-alkali unit and its styrene plant, and early in 2026 it said they were shut. Storage that served a closed unit is normally emptied, cleaned and either preserved or retired, and any tank brought back later should be evaluated before it returns to service.

Where API 653 stops: LNG tanks, spheres and shop-built tanks

The LNG terminals south of the city, Cameron LNG, Calcasieu Pass and Sabine Pass, with CP2 and Louisiana LNG Infrastructure under construction, hold some of the largest tanks in the region, but refrigerated LNG storage is built to low-temperature standards rather than to API 650, and API 653 is written for tanks built to API 650 and its predecessor API 12C. Experience on those tanks is valuable, yet it is not the same as API 653 work.

Pressurized spheres and bullets are built as pressure vessels. Where they are breakout tanks at a hazardous liquid pipeline facility built to API Std 2510, 49 CFR 195.432(c) sends them to section 6 of API 510. Small shop-built tanks are often inspected to the Steel Tank Institute's SP001 standard instead; the guide to STI SP001 and API 653 explains the split. Knowing which standard governs a tank is a recurring exam theme and the first question on any real job.

Three rulebooks that send an API 653 inspector to a Calcasieu Parish tank

  • EPA's SPCC rule. Facilities covered by the oil spill prevention rule must test or inspect each aboveground container for integrity on a regular schedule and whenever material repairs are made, under 40 CFR 112.8(c)(6), and keep records of inspections and tests for three years. EPA's fact sheet names API 653 and STI SP001 as the industry standards in common use and says that, where a field-erected tank is inspected under API 653, formal inspections are carried out by an API 653 certified inspector (SPCC integrity testing).
  • PHMSA's breakout tank rule. Under 49 CFR 195.432(b), hazardous liquid pipeline operators inspect atmospheric and low-pressure steel aboveground breakout tanks according to API Std 653, but they cannot use the risk-based internal inspection procedure that the rule cites as section 6.4.3 of the older API 653 edition it incorporates to set the internal interval. PHMSA proposed in 2026 to allow capped RBI-based intervals; until a final rule is issued, the bar stands.
  • OSHA process safety management. Storage tanks are listed with pressure vessels in the mechanical integrity paragraph of 29 CFR 1910.119, so tanks inside a covered process at a refinery or chemical plant are inspected to the good engineering practices the employer has adopted, which for welded steel tanks is usually API 653.

Low ground, heavy rain and the tank bottom

The National Weather Service's 1981 to 2010 normals put Lake Charles Regional Airport at 57.49 inches of rain a year, and much of the industrial land around the river is low and flat. For a tank inspector that combination points at the floor and the foundation. Four of the ten RP 571 mechanisms on the API 653 list for the 2027 windows live there: soil corrosion on the underside of bottom plates, microbiologically influenced corrosion where water sits under sludge or in the soil, concentration cell corrosion under deposits and at lap joints, and atmospheric corrosion at the chime where rainwater collects.

The examination expects you to know how API RP 651's cathodic protection and API RP 652's linings protect a floor, how a release prevention barrier changes the minimum floor thickness, and how to work the bottom plate minimum remaining thickness at the next inspection. Cathodic protection design itself is excluded. Soft coastal ground also makes settlement a live topic: the Body of Knowledge lists calculations for edge settlement, bottom settlement near the shell, localized settlement remote from the shell and the number of survey points, so practise all four. For floating-roof tanks, standing water and drains deserve attention after every heavy storm; the floating roof inspection guide covers what to check.

Caustic, acid and ethanol: chemical service on the API 653 list

  • Caustic corrosion and caustic stress corrosion cracking. Caustic soda storage at chlor-alkali plants, where cracking risk rises with temperature and concentration and depends on whether welds were stress relieved; heated caustic tanks with steam coils need particular care.
  • Sulfuric acid corrosion. Acid storage wherever a process uses sulfuric acid, where high velocity near nozzles and hydrogen grooving on the shell are the classic problems.
  • Ethanol stress corrosion cracking. Fuel-grade ethanol tanks at products terminals that blend gasoline.
  • Brittle fracture. Older tanks, thick shell plates and cold product, which is why API 653 and API 650 questions about design metal temperature and impact testing appear even in a warm climate.

Worked example: moving a tank into 50% caustic service

The Body of Knowledge includes evaluating the effect of a change of service on suitability for continued service, and the shell formula shows why. Specific gravity G sits directly in API 653's whole-course minimum thickness, tmin = 2.6 (H − 1) D G ÷ (S E).

  • The tank. Diameter D 60 ft, maximum fill H 40 ft above the bottom of the first course, allowable stress S of 23,600 psi for the lower courses and joint efficiency E of 1.0, both given in the problem.
  • Old service, diesel at G of about 0.85. tmin = 2.6 × 39 × 60 × 0.85 ÷ 23,600 = 0.219 in.
  • New service, 50% caustic soda at G of about 1.5. tmin = 2.6 × 39 × 60 × 1.5 ÷ 23,600 = 0.387 in.
  • Measured first course. 0.340 in., less 0.010 in. of corrosion expected before the next inspection, leaves 0.330 in. That passes comfortably in diesel and fails in caustic at full height.
  • Maximum fill height in caustic. H = S E t ÷ (2.6 D G) + 1 = 23,600 × 0.330 ÷ 234 + 1 = 34.28 ft, so about 34.2 ft rounded down.
  • Check the next course up. The second course starts 8 ft above the floor and measures 0.300 in., or 0.290 in. after the same allowance. It supports 23,600 × 0.290 ÷ 234 + 1 = 30.25 ft above its own bottom, which is 38.25 ft above the floor, so the first course still governs.

The trap is to stop after the first course or to reuse the old product's specific gravity. A real change to caustic also raises the cracking question in the previous section, which no thickness calculation answers. API 653's own formulas, including whole-course and locally thinned area checks, are worked on the API 653 course page, and the API 653 tank inspection guide explains the code's structure.

Routes into API 653 for Lake Charles tank people

Annex D of API 653 counts experience gained in the last 10 years while employed by or under contract with an authorized inspection agency, including an owner-user inspection organization. A bachelor's degree or higher in engineering or technology needs one year supervising or performing tank inspection as API 653 describes it; a two-year degree or certificate needs two years in the design, construction, repair, operation or inspection of aboveground storage tanks, one of them in supervision or performance of inspection; a high school diploma needs three; no formal education, five or more.

  • Floor scanning and UT technicians. MFL floor scans and UT prove-ups for a tank contractor are inspection work when done for an owner's programme. Atlantis's ASNT SNT-TC-1A NDT training covers UT, VT and MFL among its methods.
  • Tank repair welders and foremen. Repair and construction time counts toward the longer routes, and AWS CWI exam prep for Lake Charles candidates is a common earlier step.
  • Terminal operators. Operating experience counts toward the total but needs inspection time added.
  • Engineers. Graduates of McNeese State University's engineering programmes who join a terminal or refinery integrity group can qualify after a year of genuine inspection work.

The API 653 certification requirements page sets out the full rules.

Studying API 653 from Lake Charles, and sponsoring tank inspectors

The Body of Knowledge for the 2027 windows examines API 653 and API 650, RP 571, 575, 577, 651 and 652, part of RP 576, and ASME Section V and IX, but it excludes most API 650 annexes and limits welding questions to SMAW and GMAW on P-No. 1 base metals. Learn API 653's inspection, interval and repair rules for the closed-book half and get quick at finding API 650 tables for the open-book half. Exam day has 170 questions over 7.5 hours, 110 closed-book and 60 open-book. Prometric lists test centres in and around Lake Charles, and the window and its deadline come from the API exam schedule.

Terminals and refineries can enrol several tank inspectors under one quote, with fees quoted on request. Each candidate applies to API individually, so check experience first, choose one window, and give each person access to a certified inspector and a real tank file.

faq.q: Can I take an API 653 course in person in Lake Charles?
faq.a: No. Atlantis has no classroom in Calcasieu Parish or anywhere else. The API 653 course is self-paced and online with an instructor who answers your questions, which suits terminal and refinery schedules where tank work comes in bursts. If you want a classroom seminar, training companies run them in other cities, but they mean travel and a fixed pace.

faq.q: Does inspecting LNG storage tanks at Hackberry or Cameron count toward API 653?
faq.a: Not in the same way as work on API 650 tanks. Refrigerated LNG tanks are built to low-temperature standards, and API 653 is written for tanks built to API 650 or API 12C. Describe any experience accurately on your application and let API decide how it counts, but plan to add time on atmospheric welded steel tanks before you apply.

faq.q: Does the SPCC rule require an API 653 inspector at our terminal?
faq.a: SPCC requires each aboveground container to be tested or inspected for integrity on a regular schedule and after material repairs, following an industry standard chosen in the facility's plan. EPA's fact sheet says that where field-erected tanks are inspected under API 653, the formal inspections are done by an API 653 certified inspector. Shop-built tanks are often handled under STI SP001 instead.

faq.q: Can a pipeline terminal use RBI to stretch a breakout tank's internal inspection interval?
faq.a: No. Federal rules at 49 CFR 195.432(b) require hazardous liquid pipeline operators to inspect their atmospheric and low-pressure steel breakout tanks to API Std 653 but bar them from using the risk-based internal inspection procedure the rule cites as section 6.4.3 of the API 653 edition it incorporates. Refinery tanks outside pipeline jurisdiction are not bound by that limit. PHMSA published a proposal in 2026 that would allow capped RBI intervals for breakout tanks, but until a final rule is issued the bar stands.

faq.q: I run MFL floor scans for a tank contractor. How far am I from API 653 eligibility?
faq.a: It depends on your education and on whether your scans and prove-ups were performed for owners' inspection programmes while you were employed by or contracted to an authorized inspection agency. With a high school diploma API asks for three years of tank experience including one in supervision or performance of inspection. Keep a record of tanks, dates and methods, because API verifies it.

faq.q: Are settlement calculations on the API 653 exam?
faq.a: Yes. The 2027 Body of Knowledge lists edge settlement, bottom settlement near the shell, localized settlement remote from the shell and the number of survey points among the examined calculations. On the soft, low-lying ground around Lake Charles these are also everyday questions on real tanks, so it pays to learn the Annex B methods properly rather than memorise one worked answer.

faq.q: Which parts of API 650 should I study for API 653?
faq.a: Focus on the parts used when tanks are repaired, altered or reconstructed: materials, impact testing and design metal temperature, shell design, weld sizes for openings, joint efficiency and inspection of welds. The Body of Knowledge excludes most API 650 annexes, keeping only the opening clauses of a few, so do not spend weeks on annexes you will not be examined on.

faq.q: Can a terminal operator enrol several tank inspectors together?
faq.a: Yes. A terminal, refinery or tank contractor can sponsor a group under one quote, and fees are quoted on request. Each person still applies to API individually with their own experience record, so check eligibility before enrolment and choose a single exam window for the group.
